title: Tone-label agreement with per-project quorum
scenario: Per-project batches of tone labels are deduped, resolved to agreed/escalated/pending against each project's quorum and agreement bar, then scored per annotator and summarised per project and per team (roster CSV has a BOM).

verified.why_correct: The `>=` looks like it might need to be `>`, but README rule 5 says a share at or above the bar is agreed (C-01 is exactly 3/4 = 0.75). The explicit tie check implements rule 4, so R-01's 2-2 split escalates even though 0.5 meets the reviews bar.
The day.month.year format looks like it clashes with month/day/year, but the separators differ (`.` vs `/`), so each string matches exactly one format, and both are listed in the README.

bugs.title: Resubmissions not collapsed
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_vote_counts: C-04 shows 5 votes (expected 4) and E-06 shows 4 (expected 3). Every status and label is still right.
bugs.why: The dedupe helper is never called, so a09's two C-04 rows and a11's two E-06 rows are both counted as votes. Neither task changes status, so only the vote counts show it.
hints: Pick C-04 and count its rows in chat.csv by annotator. Who appears twice?
Follow load_annotations: where is rule 1 applied?
probes: Why didn't C-04's status change even though it got an extra vote?
If a09 had changed their label on the resubmission, which other tests could have failed?

bugs.title: Exactly min_votes treated as too few
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_statuses: C-03, E-01 and R-01 are 'pending' instead of 'escalated'. Each has exactly its project's min_votes votes.
bugs.why: Rule 3 says exactly min_votes is enough to decide. `<=` sends every task with exactly the quorum to pending. In this data all of those tasks are escalated (C-03, E-01, R-01), so only the status map changes.
hints: Compare the vote counts of the tasks that went to pending with each project's min_votes.
Look at the quorum check in resolve().
probes: Why did no agreed label change even though three tasks changed status?
Which data row would you add to make this change agreement rates too?

bugs.title: Skips counted as disagreeing votes
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_agreement_rates: a06 shows agreed_tasks 5 / agreement 0.8 (expected 4 / 1.0) and a08 shows 6 / 0.333 (expected 4 / 0.5). Skip counts are right.
bugs.why: Without the `continue`, a skip on an agreed task falls through and is counted as a vote that didn't match. a06 (skipped R-03) and a08 (skipped C-07 and E-05) get extra agreed_tasks and lower agreement.
hints: Only a06 and a08 are off. What else do they have in common in the table?
Trace a skip row through agreement_table's loop.
probes: Why are a02's numbers right even though a02 also skipped a task?
Why do skip counts still come out right?

bugs.title: Zero agreement reported as None
bugs.old: round(row.rate, 3) if row.rate is not None else None
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_low_and_unscored_annotators: a10 shows agreement None (expected 0.0) even though agreed_tasks is 4.
bugs.why: a10 disagreed on all 4 agreed tasks, so the rate is 0.0. A truthiness check treats 0.0 like a missing rate and prints None, which the spec reserves for annotators with no agreed tasks.
hints: a10 has agreed_tasks 4 but no agreement value. Is that consistent with rule 7?
Look at how the rate is formatted for the report.
probes: Why does a11 still correctly show None?
Where else in this repo could a 0 be confused with missing?

bugs.title: Per-project label counts accumulate
bugs.new:
def count_labels(results, counts=Counter()):
    """Add the agreed labels in `results` to `counts` (a fresh Counter by default)."""
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_labels_by_project: the per-project counts keep growing (in a full-suite run chat shows negative 7, neutral 4, positive 13). The overall counts are right.
bugs.why: The default Counter is created once, when the function is defined, so every call without `counts` adds to the same object. Each project's breakdown includes the projects before it (and earlier build_report calls). The overall count passes its own Counter, so it stays right.
hints: The overall counts are right but per-project counts keep growing. What do the two paths share?
Default `counts=None` and create the Counter inside the function.
probes: Why does running test_3 alone give different numbers from running the whole suite?

bugs.title: Roster read without stripping the BOM
bugs.old: with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
bugs.new: with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_team_summary: teams comes back as {} (expected east/north/south/west with members and votes).
bugs.why: teams.csv starts with a UTF-8 BOM. Read as plain utf-8, the first header becomes '\ufeffannotator_id', so `row.get("annotator_id")` is None for every row and the roster comes back empty. The batch files have no BOM, so nothing else changes.
hints: The roster loads with no members. Print the keys of the first row read_rows returns for teams.csv.
Compare how teams.csv is decoded with what the README says about it.
probes: Why didn't `.strip()` on the header remove the mark?
Why were the batch CSVs unaffected even though they use the same reader?

context_qa.q: What does build_report() do, step by step?
context_qa.a: It loads projects.json, reads every batch CSV whose stem is a project (`load_annotations`), resolves each task (`consensus.resolve`), builds the per-annotator table (`agreement.agreement_table`), counts agreed labels per project and overall (`label_breakdown`), and builds the team summary from teams.csv plus each annotator's vote count.
A list of dicts, one per CSV data row. Each column name is passed through `clean()` and lower-cased, and each cell is trimmed. It is used for the batch files and for teams.csv.

context_qa.q: How does a skip row flow through the code?
context_qa.a: The loader keeps it as an Annotation with label 'skip'; `Annotation.skipped` is True for it. `resolve` leaves skips out of a task's labels but still records the task's project, and `votes_by_annotator` leaves them out. In `agreement_table`, a skip increments that annotator's `skips` counter.

context_qa.q: Where does a task's project come from?
context_qa.a: From the batch file name: `load_annotations` passes `norm_id(path.stem)` to `read_batch`, which stamps it on each Annotation. `resolve` remembers the last project seen for each task id.

context_qa.q: How is the label breakdown built?
context_qa.a: `label_breakdown` loops over project ids in sorted order, filters results to that project, and calls `count_labels(rows)` for the per-project dict and `count_labels(rows, overall)` to add to the overall Counter.

context_qa.q: What does load_teams do with each roster row?
context_qa.a: It reads rows with `read_rows`, takes `row.get("annotator_id")` and `row.get("team")`, normalises both with `norm_id`, and keeps the row only if the annotator id is non-empty. The result maps annotator id to team.

context_qa.q: Which annotators appear in the annotators table?
context_qa.a: Every annotator id that appears in the deduped annotations, whether the rows are votes or skips, sorted by id.
